claims.statement: Per-user preferences are stored in exactly one nullable JSON column, `UserModel.preferences` on `auth_users`, added by the Alembic revision 1548d7b88af5 and mirrored as `UserSchema.preferences`; there is one document per user and nothing is keyed by security, route, or device.

The preferences surface is GET, PUT and PATCH on `/accounts/me/preferences`, mounted under `/api/v1` by `src/main.py`; GET returns `{}` when nothing is saved, and all three endpoints depend on `current_user` so an unauthenticated request returns 401.

The request payload model `UserPreferences` uses `model_config = ConfigDict(extra="allow")` and declares only a subset of the keys the frontend uses, so unknown keys round-trip through storage unchanged while declared fields are still type-validated; the backend declaration is therefore advisory and the authoritative key list lives in the frontend interface and its writers.

Both write verbs dump with `exclude_none=True`, so an explicit JSON null is never persisted and cannot clear a stored key: PUT replaces the whole document (a partial PUT body is a replace, not a merge), while PATCH can only add or overwrite non-null top-level keys.

PATCH performs a top-level-only merge by assigning `coalesce(cast(preferences, JSONB), cast({}, JSONB)).op("||")(cast(payload, JSONB))` with `RETURNING preferences`, which makes nested objects such as `indicators`, `wave_settings`, `elliott_waves` and `holdings_table` whole-value keys and makes one-key-per-write the race-safe shape for independently mounted components.

`UserPreferencesService` in `frontend/src/lib/api/userPreferencesService.ts` is the only client of the endpoint, extending `ApiClient` with `getPreferences`, `savePreferences` (PUT) and `patchPreferences` (PATCH); it is exported as `getUserPreferencesService(customFetch)` for SSR loads that inject the server `fetch` and pass the `auth_token` cookie via the token override, and as a module singleton for browser components.

The root layout load (`frontend/src/routes/+layout.server.ts`) reads exactly `sidebar_open`, `collapsed_watchlist_ids` and `watchlist_order` on every authenticated request, guarding each with a type check and defaulting to `true`, `[]` and `null`, and swallows any request failure so layout hydration never fails on a preferences outage.

The `/holdings` server load reads `holdings_table`, `holdings_group` and `elliott_waves` inside its own `try/catch` and treats a preferences failure as non-fatal, returning `normalizeHoldingsTableConfig(null)`, `'none'` and `null` waves while holdings rows still load after navigation; the `/watchlists` load reads no preference at all (returning `{ watchlists: [] }`) and the security route load returns only `security_id`, with the page fetching preferences client-side.

Persistence failure handling differs per surface: layout and sidebar writes are fire-and-forget (`patchPreferences(...).catch(console.error)`), the `/holdings` page captures rejections into a page-level `persistError` rendered in a destructive alert, the `/watchlists` reorder path rolls the optimistic order back and sets `watchlistService.error`, and the security page and `ChartDrawingsService` writes only log.

`ChartDrawingsService` is the only writer of the `elliott_waves`, `fibonacci_tools` and `drawings` keys, patching them from wave/fib/drawing change handlers, the undo/redo restore path and the deferred drag-end flush, and it reads them back through per-security getters keyed by security id.

Two declared preference keys have no consumer: `sidebar_watchlists` exists only in the frontend interface, and `watchlist_sort` is declared on the backend model and covered by a router test but is not read by any frontend code, because per-watchlist security sort moved to the `WatchlistRead.sort` column persisted through `PATCH /market/watchlists/{id}`.

`mergeChartPreferences` in `frontend/src/lib/chart-preferences.ts` is a tested read-merge-write helper that preserves the `indicators` key across partial writes, but no production code calls it: the security page's `updateChartPreferences` issues a bare partial PATCH and relies on the server's top-level merge.

Because `extra="allow"` lets unvalidated values into the column, robustness lives in the readers: `normalizeHoldingsTableConfig` drops unknown column ids, clamps widths to per-column bounds and forces the sticky first column visible, `normalizeHoldingsGroupMode` maps anything that is not `stock`/`company` to `'none'`, and `holdings-modal.svelte` rejects a stored `holdings_period` outside its `PERIODS` list in favour of `ALL`.

Per-security indicator preferences were removed in favour of the user-global `indicators` key: the `market_indicator_preferences` table and its `GET|PUT /market/securities/{id}/indicator-preferences` endpoints are gone, and a regression test asserts those routes return 404.

Whole-key writers always send the complete value because a PATCH replaces the key: `handlePaneHeightsChange` sends the full pane-height map (or null), `handleWaveSettingsChange` sends the whole settings object, and `IndicatorsGroup` sends the entire `indicators` map on toggle, settings save and reset.

A failed preferences read is never fatal and is load-bearing for wave alerts: the security page leaves `userPreferences` null on a fetch failure and gates the initial wave-alert reconcile on preferences having loaded, so a preference outage cannot mass-delete wave-target alerts.
`holdings_period` is read by `holdings-modal.svelte` on every modal open (not by the route loads) and written by the period selector through a fire-and-forget patch that only logs failures.

`tests/routers/test_accounts.py` is the backend contract test suite for preferences: it pins the empty-document response, PUT/GET round-trip, partial-update-without-fabricated-defaults, cross-component PATCH isolation, per-user isolation in both directions, and per-key round-trips for `sidebar_open`, `holdings_period`, `elliott_waves`, `fibonacci_tools`, `wave_settings` and `watchlist_order`/`watchlist_sort`.
